docs.title: Home
docs.text: Recos is a recruitment platform that integrates seamlessly with Odoo and Google Calendar—powered by advanced AI for interviews, reporting, and hiring analytics.

docs.title: Why Choose Recos?
docs.text:
• Next-Gen AI: Automated candidate assessment, interview question generation, and detailed analytics.
  • Odoo Integration: Instantly connect, sync jobs/candidates, and manage all recruitment data in one place.
  • Google Calendar/Meet: Effortless interview scheduling with automatic Meet link generation.
  • Real-Time Transcription: AssemblyAI integration for live interview transcription and Gemini analytics.
  • Tech Stack: Next.js, Tailwind CSS, TypeScript, Django REST. Deployed with Vercel CI/CD.
  • API-First: All features accessible via tested REST APIs (see API Reference).

docs.title: Frontend Standards (Next.js, TypeScript, Tailwind)
docs.text:
Components

  • Always use functional components for consistency and performance.

Example:

// Good
export function UserCard({ name }: { name: string }) {
  return <div>{name}</div>;
}

// Avoid
class UserCard extends React.Component {
  render() {
    return <div>{this.props.name}</div>;
  }
}

Naming Conventions

  • camelCase for variables and functions const userName = 'Jacky'; function getUserData() {}
  • PascalCase for component names function UserProfile() {}

Styling

  • Use Tailwind CSS for all styling.

docs.title: General Standards
docs.text:
Keep Functions and Components Small & Focused

  • Each function/component should do one thing only.
  • Aim for less than 50 lines per function/component.
  • Split complex logic into smaller utility functions.

Benefits:

  • Improves readability and maintainability
  • Easier to test and debug
  • Logic is reusable across other components

1. Handling Commented-Out Code

  • Do not commit commented-out code unless it clarifies complex logic or algorithms.
  • Remove commented code as soon as it is no longer necessary.

2. Lint & Test Before Every Commit

  • Run all linters and automated tests before every commit (not just before merging).
  • If tests or linting fail, resolve errors before committing.

3. Follow Naming & File Organization Conventions

  • Use camelCase, PascalCase, and snake_case as specified.
  • Organize files by feature/module for easier navigation and maintenance.

4. Write Clear Commit Messages & PR Summaries

  • Each commit/PR should explain what changed and why.
  • Reference any related issues.

5. General Workflow Expectations

  • Always branch from the latest develop branch and open PRs into develop (not main).
  • Test changes locally before pushing.
  • Request code review before merging.

docs.title: Frontend Deployment
docs.text:
Platform: Vercel

Deployment Branch: Auto-deployment is enabled from the main branch. Only merges to main trigger a production deployment. --

Pre-Deployment (Local Build): Before pushing code, always run a local production build to catch issues early:

npm run build

Build & Preview Process:

  • Each push or pull request (PR) automatically triggers a Vercel preview build.
  • Preview URLs are available both in the PR (on GitHub) and in the Vercel dashboard.
  • Merging to the main branch triggers a production deployment.
  • To view a build preview, open your PR on GitHub and look for the "Vercel Preview" check.

Failure:

  • If deployment fails, review build logs and errors in the Vercel dashboard under "Deployments."
  • Resolve any issues and push a new commit to trigger a redeployment.
  • To rollback, revert the main branch to a previous working commit and redeploy.

docs.title: Backend Deployment
docs.text:
Platform: Heroku

Deployment Trigger and Access: The admin deploys after merging all approved PRs to develop and then to main. Only the admin and one developer have Heroku access. The developer can view logs only; only the admin can deploy.

Pre-Deployment (Local Build/Test): Before deploying, always run local tests and collect static files:

python manage.py test
python manage.py collectstatic

Manual Steps: If the deployment includes database schema changes, run migrations:

heroku run python manage.py migrate --app <heroku-app-name>

Check for migration errors and confirm data integrity.

Failure If deployment fails, check logs using:

heroku logs --tail --app <heroku-app-name>

Fix issues and redeploy.

docs.title: CI/CD Pipeline
docs.text:
Tool: GitHub Actions

Workflow: Every push and PR triggers automated tests (unit and integration), builds, and lint/code quality checks. If all checks pass, code can be merged and deployed.

Deployment Automation: On merge to main, GitHub Actions triggers production deployments for frontend (to Vercel) and backend (Heroku). Build/test status is visible on PRs and in the GitHub Actions tab.

Failure Handling: If a workflow fails, check logs in the Actions tab, fix issues, and re-run as needed.

docs.title: General Deployment Checklist
docs.text:
1. Ensure all code is reviewed and merged into the appropriate branch.
  2. Confirm all required environment variables are documented and set in their dashboards.
  3. Run all tests locally before pushing code.
  4. Monitor the deployment process using Vercel/Heroku dashboards and/or GitHub Actions.
  5. After deployment, verify the application by running manual checks or automated post-deploy checks.

docs.title: How Recos Platform Works
docs.text:
Recos is an AI-powered recruitment assistant designed to streamline hiring, increase accuracy, and support fair candidate assessment for recruiters.

The platform integrates deeply with Odoo ATS and leverages advanced AI for interviews, analytics, and reporting.

docs.title:
1. Recruiter Registration & Authentication
  • Sign Up: Recruiters create an account using their first name, last name, email, and password.
  • Login: After registration, recruiters log in with their credentials.
  • Password Reset: If a recruiter forgets their password, they can request a reset. A code is sent to their email, allowing them to set a new password securely.

2. Odoo Integration & Account Verification
  • After logging in, recruiters connect their Odoo account by providing:
  • Odoo instance URL
  • Email
  • API key
  • Credentials are verified directly with Odoo, ensuring secure access to candidate and job data.

3. Company Selection & Dashboard Access
  • Recruiters are presented with a list of companies (fetched from Odoo) they are associated with.
  • After selecting a company, the recruiter lands on the dashboard, where they can:
  • View job postings for the selected company
  • See candidates who have applied to those jobs

4. Candidate Profile Management
  • For each candidate, Recos automatically generates a structured profile, including:
  • Skills
  • Qualifications
  • Experience
  • All candidate profiles are stored within the platform, making it easy for recruiters to review, search, and manage candidates efficiently.

5. Interview Scheduling
  • Recruiters can schedule interviews by selecting a candidate and setting a date/time.
  • The system generates and sends a Google Meet link to the candidate (via Google Calendar integration).

6. AI-Assisted Interview Process
  • Pre-Interview Preparation: The AI analyzes both the candidate’s CV/profile and the job description, building a knowledge base of required versus offered skills.
  • During the Interview:
  • Recruiter and candidate join the interview via the Google Meet link.
  • Recos AI transparently joins, with the recruiter signaling when to start.
  • The AI dynamically generates tailored questions based on the candidate’s background and job requirements.
  • It adapts in real-time, asking follow-up questions for deeper insights.

  • All speech is transcribed using Google Speech-to-Text AI.

  • Recos AI Add-on:

  • The recruiter receives dynamically generated interview questions and prompts through the platform’s interface.
  • Post-Interview Reporting:
  • After the interview, Gemini AI generates a detailed report that:
    • Summarizes how well the candidate demonstrated required skills
    • Identifies strengths and gaps
    • Provides actionable insights for decision-making

7. Odoo Data Sync
  • Odoo serves as the trusted source for recruiter accounts, job descriptions, and CVs.
  • The platform syncs candidate and job data with Odoo to ensure accuracy and timeliness.
Why Recos Is Valuable
docs.text:
• Saves recruiters’ time: Pre-validates candidate claims before the interview stage.
  • Increases hiring accuracy: Reduces resume exaggeration or misrepresentation.
  • Enables fairer assessments: Objectively tests practical and behavioral skills.
  • Improves candidate matching: Ensures fit with role requirements based on actual demonstrated abilities.

docs.title: Typical Recruiter Journey in Recos
docs.text:
1. Sign Up → Login → Odoo Connect
  2. Select Company → Explore Jobs & Candidates
  3. Schedule Interview → AI-Assisted Interview → Candidate Report
  4. Data remains synced with Odoo for up-to-date profiles and job listings

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text: Welcome to the platform! This section guides you through account creation, authentication, password reset flows, and connecting your Odoo account. Each step includes technical details and backend logic.

docs.title: 1. Sign Up
docs.text:
To create a new account, fill out the following fields:

  • First Name
  • Last Name
  • Email
  • Password

How it works: - The backend creates a new user record after validating the fields. - Passwords are securely hashed.

POST   /api/signup

Sample Request (Frontend → Backend):

{
  "first_name": "Jacky",
  "last_name": "Uwase",
  "email": "jacky@gmail.com",
  "password": "Kumany1@"
}

Sample Response:

{
  "message": "Account created successfully."
}

Backend Logic:

from rest_framework.views import APIView
from rest_framework.response import Response
from rest_framework import status
from django.contrib.auth.models import User
from django.contrib.auth.hashers import make_password

class SignUpView(APIView):
    def post(self, request):
        first_name = request.data.get('first_name')
        last_name = request.data.get('last_name')
        email = request.data.get('email')
        password = request.data.get('password')
        if not (first_name and last_name and email and password):
            return Response({'error': 'All fields are required.'}, status=status.HTTP_400_BAD_REQUEST)
        if User.objects.filter(email=email).exists():
            return Response({'error': 'Email already exists.'}, status=status.HTTP_400_BAD_REQUEST)
        user = User.objects.create(
            first_name=first_name,
            last_name=last_name,
            email=email,
            username=email,
            password=make_password(password)
        )
        return Response({'message': 'Account created successfully.'}, status=status.HTTP_201_CREATED)

docs.title: 2. Login
docs.text:
If you already have an account, sign in using:

  • Email
  • Password
POST   /api/login

Sample Request:

{
  "email": "jacky@gmail.com",
  "password": "Kumany1@"
}

Sample Response:

{
  "token": "jwt-token"
}

Backend Logic:

from rest_framework_simplejwt.tokens import RefreshToken

class LoginView(APIView):
    def post(self, request):
        email = request.data.get('email')
        password = request.data.get('password')
        user = authenticate(username=email, password=password)
        if user is not None:
            refresh = RefreshToken.for_user(user)
            return Response({'token': str(refresh.access_token)})
        return Response({'error': 'Invalid credentials.'}, status=status.HTTP_401_UNAUTHORIZED)

docs.title: 3. Forgot Password Flow
docs.text: If you forget your password, follow these steps:

docs.title: a. Initiate Password Reset
docs.text:
• Click "Forgot Password?" on the login page.
  • Enter your registered email address.
POST   /forgot-password/          # Start password reset

Sample Request:

{
  "email": "jacky@gmail.com"
}

Sample Response:

{
  "message": "Password reset code sent."
}

Backend Logic:

class ForgotPasswordView(APIView):
    permission_classes = [permissions.AllowAny]

    def post(self, request):
        email = request.data.get('email', '').lower().strip()
        if not email:
            return Response({'error': 'Email is required'}, status=status.HTTP_400_BAD_REQUEST)

        try:
            user = Recruiter.objects.get(email=email)
        except Recruiter.DoesNotExist:
            return Response({'message': 'Password reset code sent if email exists in our system'}, status=status.HTTP_200_OK)

        verification_code = ''.join(random.choices('0123456789', k=4))
        cache.set(f'reset_code_{email}', verification_code, timeout=3*60)

        subject = 'Password Reset Verification Code'
        message = (
            f"Hello {user.first_name},\n\n"
            f"We received a request to reset your password. Use the verification code below:\n\n"
            f"{verification_code}\n\n"
            f"This code will expire in 3 minutes.\n\n"
            f"If you didn't request this, please ignore this email.\n\n"
            f"Thank you,\nThe Team"
        )

        send_mail(subject, message, settings.DEFAULT_FROM_EMAIL, [user.email], fail_silently=False)
        return Response({'message': 'Password reset code sent.'}, status=status.HTTP_200_OK)

docs.title: b. Enter Verification Code
docs.text:
After receiving an email, enter the 4-digit code on the verification page.

POST   /verify-reset-code/        # Verify reset code sent to email

Sample Request:

{
  "email": "jacky@gmail.com",
  "code": "1234"
}

Sample Response:

{
  "detail": "Code verified, you may now reset your password."
}

Backend Logic:

class VerifyCodeView(APIView):
    permission_classes = [permissions.AllowAny]

    def post(self, request):
        email = request.data.get('email', '').lower().strip()
        code = str(request.data.get('code', '')).strip()
        if not email or not code:
            return Response({'detail': 'Email and code are required.'}, status=status.HTTP_400_BAD_REQUEST)

        cached_code = cache.get(f'reset_code_{email}')
        if cached_code is None:
            return Response({"detail": "Code has expired, please request a new one."}, status=status.HTTP_400_BAD_REQUEST)
        if cached_code != code:
            return Response({"detail": "Invalid code."}, status=status.HTTP_400_BAD_REQUEST)

        request.session['reset_email'] = email
        cache.delete(f'reset_code_{email}')
        return Response({"detail": "Code verified, you may now reset your password."})

docs.title: c. Reset Password
docs.text:
After code verification, set a new password (two fields: New Password, Confirm New Password).

POST   /reset-password/           # Complete password reset

Sample Request:

{
  "email": "jacky@gmail.com",
  "password": "NewStrong1@"
}

Sample Response:

{
  "detail": "Password reset successful."
}

Backend Logic:

class ResetPasswordView(APIView):
    permission_classes = [AllowAny] 

    def post(self, request):
        serializer = ResetPasswordSerializer(data=request.data)
        serializer.is_valid(raise_exception=True)
        email = serializer.validated_data['email']
        password = serializer.validated_data['password']
        try:
            user = User.objects.get(email=email)
        except User.DoesNotExist:
            return Response({"detail": "User with this email does not exist."}, status=status.HTTP_400_BAD_REQUEST)
        user.set_password(password)
        user.save()
        code_storage.pop(email, None)
        return Response({"detail": "Password reset successful."})

docs.title: 4. Connecting to Odoo
docs.text:
After logging in, connect your Odoo account using:

  • Odoo Instance URL
  • Email
  • API Key / Password
POST   /api/connect-odoo

Sample Request:

{
  "odoo_url": "https://your-odoo-instance.com",
  "email": "odoo_user@example.com",
  "api_key": "yourOdooApiKey"
}

Sample Response:

{
  "companies": [
    {
      "id": 1,
      "name": "Acme Corp"
    },
    {
      "id": 2,
      "name": "Innovate LLC"
    }
  ]
}

Backend Logic:

import requests

class ConnectOdooView(APIView):
    def post(self, request):
        odoo_url = request.data.get('odoo_url')
        email = request.data.get('email')
        api_key = request.data.get('api_key')
        if not (odoo_url and email and api_key):
            return Response({'error': 'All fields are required.'}, status=status.HTTP_400_BAD_REQUEST)
        # Example Odoo connection logic (pseudo)
        response = requests.post(f"{odoo_url}/api/auth", data={"email": email, "api_key": api_key})
        if response.status_code != 200:
            return Response({'error': 'Odoo authentication failed.'}, status=status.HTTP_401_UNAUTHORIZED)
        # Fetch companies
        companies = requests.get(f"{odoo_url}/api/companies", headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {api_key}"})
        return Response({'companies': companies.json()}, status=status.HTTP_200_OK)

docs.title: Odoo Integration
docs.text:
Purpose in Recos: Odoo integration is central to Recos. It enables recruiters to connect their Odoo account and manage jobs, candidates, and company data directly from the platform. All recruiter authentication, job and candidate data, and company information are trusted and synced from Odoo, ensuring accuracy and up-to-date records.

Where is it used?

  • Authenticating recruiter accounts (via Odoo credentials)
  • Fetching jobs, companies, and candidate profiles
  • Keeping candidate/job data synced between Odoo and Recos

### Setup

- Obtain your Odoo Instance URL (e.g., `https://your-odoo-instance.com`)
- Generate an API Key in Odoo (Settings → API Keys)

ODOO_URL=https://your-odoo-instance.com ODOO_EMAIL=your@email.com ODOO_API_KEY=yourapikey


### Example: Connecting via API

```python
import requests

url = f"{ODOO_URL}/api/jobs"
headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {ODOO_API_KEY}"}
response = requests.get(url, headers=headers)
print(response.json())

• GET /odoo/jobs — Fetch jobs
  • GET /odoo/candidates — Fetch candidates

docs.title: Google Calendar & Google Meet Integration
docs.text:

  • Send out invites to candidates
  • Ensure seamless virtual meetings

Where is it used?

  • Scheduling interviews with candidates
  • Generating and sending Google Meet links via calendar invites

docs.title: OAuth 2.0 Client Credentials
docs.text:
• Go to APIs & Services → Credentials

docs.text:
from google_auth_oauthlib.flow import Flow

flow = Flow.from_client_secrets_file(
    'credentials.json',
    scopes=['https://www.googleapis.com/auth/calendar'],
    redirect_uri='https://your-domain.com/api/auth/google/callback/'
)
authorization_url, state = flow.authorization_url(access_type='offline', prompt='consent')

docs.title: Google Speech-to-Text Integration
docs.text:
Purpose in Recos: This integration transcribes interviews in real time, converting audio from Google Meet calls into text. Transcriptions are used for further AI analysis, reporting, and generating interview insights.

Where is it used?

  • During the interview: All recruiter and candidate speech is transcribed.
  • After the interview: Transcripts are sent to Gemini AI for analysis and report generation.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
• Enable Google Cloud Speech-to-Text API in your Google Cloud project
  • Obtain API key and store in .env

docs.title: Store API Key (.env)
docs.text: GOOGLE_SPEECH_TO_TEXT_API_KEY=your_api_key

docs.title: Transcribe Interview Audio (Python Example)
docs.text:
import requests

audio_file = open('interview_audio.wav', 'rb')
headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {GOOGLE_SPEECH_TO_TEXT_API_KEY}"}
response = requests.post(
    "https://speech.googleapis.com/v1/speech:recognize",
    headers=headers,
    data=audio_file
)
transcript_text = response.json()['results'][0]['alternatives'][0]['transcript']

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
• Only store and transmit audio securely
  • Delete audio files after transcription to preserve privacy

docs.title: Gemini Integration (AI Reports & Question Generation)
docs.text:
Purpose in Recos: Gemini AI integration powers two essential features in the Recos platform:

  • Interview Add-on (Question Generation): Gemini analyzes candidate CVs and job descriptions to dynamically generate tailored interview questions and follow-up prompts during the interview.

  • AI Reports: After the interview, Gemini produces a detailed report that analyzes the transcript and candidate performance. This includes sentiment analysis, skill demonstration, identification of strengths and gaps, and final recommendations for the recruiter.

Where is it used?

  • Pre-interview: Generating interview questions based on job requirements and candidate profiles.
  • During interview: Adapting questions and probing deeper into candidate responses in real time.
  • Post-interview: Generating AI-powered reports for recruiter decision support.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
• Enable Gemini API on Google AI Platform
  • Obtain API key and set quotas

docs.title: Store API Key (.env)
docs.text: GEMINI_API_KEY=your_api_key

docs.title: Example: Sending Data to Gemini for Analysis
docs.text:
import requests

headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {GEMINI_API_KEY}"}
data = {
    "interview_text": transcript_text, 
    "candidate_profile": {...},
    "job_description": {...}
}
response = requests.post("https://gemini.googleapis.com/v1/analyze", json=data, headers=headers)
report = response.json()

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
• Limit the amount of personal data sent for analysis
  • Use secure HTTPS endpoints for all Gemini API calls
  • Document and review how AI-generated insights are presented to recruiters

docs.title: General Troubleshooting & Best Practices
docs.text:
• Always use .env for all secrets—never commit credentials or sensitive files.
  • Rotate API keys regularly and restrict access by least privilege.
  • Encrypt sensitive files (credentials.json, audio files) and store securely.
  • Monitor integration logs and error reports to diagnose issues quickly.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
Backend Unit Tests

All backend tests should include normal use, edge cases, and error handling.

How to run and check tests:

python manage.py test

Example:

from django.test import TestCase
from .models import Item

class ItemModelTest(TestCase):
    def test_str(self):
        item = Item.objects.create(name="Test Item")
        self.assertEqual(str(item), "Test Item")

Frontend Testing

All UI components must have automated tests using Jest + React Testing Library, as well as manual validation.

How to run tests:

npm run test

Example:

import { render, screen } from '@testing-library/react';
import Button from './Button';

test('renders with label', () => {
  render(<Button label="Click me" />);
  expect(screen.getByText('Click me')).toBeInTheDocument();
});

For every new feature, fill out the manual testing checklist.

API Testing

All API endpoints must be tested using Postman collections. Update Postman tests as endpoints change.

docs.title: Example workflow
docs.text:
• Create a Postman request to /api/users/
  • Check for status 200 and correct response JSON.
  • Run the full Postman collection before major merges.

docs.title: Postman API Documentation
docs.text:
• Always keep API documentation up to date with code changes.
  • Update docs after adding, changing, or removing endpoints.
  • View Postman Documentation
